defects.behavior: Choosing a sort order does not reorder the product list (error_user also shows an alert).
"Add to cart" for Sauce Labs Bolt T-Shirt does not add it (no cart badge).
"Remove" for Sauce Labs Backpack does not remove it (badge stays).
Typing a last name writes into the first-name field; checkout cannot continue.
The last-name field ignores input and the missing last name is not reported; checkout continues.
Finish does not complete the order.
Creating a note (API or form) fails with 500.
Any signed-in user can read, change and delete other users' notes (200 instead of 403).
Titles longer than 120 characters are accepted (201 instead of 400).

limitations: 0 of 104 reference labels are human-reviewed; the rest are assigned by the framework author, who also wrote the rules they score, and are pending review.
Datasets are small: rates with fewer than 10 cases in the denominator are marked insufficient-data, and percentiles from fewer than 20 samples are not distributions.
The test target is a public demo site with no version identifier; seeded defects are its intentionally broken accounts, verified by eval/probes/seeded-defects.ts.

The failure classifier treats an expected value as coming from the requirement when it appears anywhere in the criterion text (substring), which can turn an incorrect assertion into a product_behavior diagnosis.
Live-provider evaluation has not been run in this repository (no credentials); no model-quality, token or cost figures exist yet.
Functional mode executes pinned hand-written candidate specs; detection rates describe those specs and the pipeline, not what a model would generate.
Functional runs use a 15 s test timeout (stricter than the policy) so stuck pages fail fast.
